subject: owl
pitch: A great horned owl perched on a gnarled branch. Mottled bark-brown and buff feathers with fine dark barring, a pale bib at the throat, tall feathered ear tufts, a round tawny facial disc rimmed in black, huge orange eyes and a hooked grey beak. Feathered legs end in strong black talons gripping the wood.
reasoning:
I'm planning a three.js scene for a great horned owl perched on a gnarled branch, sketching out proportions and the stylized body shape using scaled sphere primitives in brown-buff tones.

I'm mapping out facial disc, eyes, hooked beak, ear tufts, layered folded wings with barring, tail, and legs with gripping talons, plus a canvas-generated texture for feather barring and mottling that I'll apply to the materials.

I'm using a seeded random generator for branch twig variation, positioning the owl facing +Z on a gnarled horizontal branch so its talons wrap over the top where the branch meets the ground plane, and working out the body proportions from feet height up through the torso to the ear tufts.

Now I'm scaling the whole figure down to a more realistic owl height of roughly 0.6 units, adjusting leg, body, and head center points so each segment overlaps naturally, then building the facial disc as a flattened sphere with a torus rim facing forward on the head.

Placing the eyes as large orange spheres with black pupils and thin dark rims, adding a hooked cone beak with a small tip sphere for the hook shape, a buff-colored bib sphere under the beak, and angled ear-tuft cones tilted outward near the top of the head.

Now I'm shaping the folded wings as elongated ellipsoids on each side with stacked feather layers hanging down, a tilted flattened box tail angled down-back toward the branch, feathered thigh spheres and tarsus cylinders for the legs, and small black curved talon cones gripping the branch at each foot.

I'm positioning the branch as a horizontal cylinder with its top aligned to the feet height, adding knots and twig stubs for texture, then building a procedural canvas texture for buff-brown mottled barring to apply across the body material, and setting up emissive-tinted eye materials for the pupils. Now I'm starting the actual code, importing Three.js, defining the owl's metadata, and setting up a seeded random number generator for texture variation.

Writing bark texture generator...

Simplifying wings to layered feather ellipsoids stacked with a shared textured material, then working out talon geometry: toe groups rotated around the foot position with cones flipped to point downward for claws.

Simplifying talon placement...

Now I'm setting up the branch geometry as a tilted cylinder with a thicker base, adding small gnarl bumps and dark knot spheres, plus a thin twig angled upward so it doesn't overlap the owl positioned at the branch's center.

Thinking about proportions, I want the owl to stay upright and simple rather than leaning, with talons sinking slightly into the branch surface for grounding. For the face, I'm placing the facial disc, eye rings, and pupils as layered depth positions along the z-axis so the eyes sit mostly within the disc but protrude just enough to read clearly from the front.

Now I'm working out the beak as a cone with a small hooked tip cone angled downward, and adding a secondary buff-white bib ellipsoid positioned to overhang the body's curved surface for a layered chest look. I'm also setting texture repeat on the body material and finalizing feathered thigh spheres before writing out the complete code with proper metadata.
